PSHE and RSE
The government has made it compulsory that Relationship Education is taught at primary school. This is so the building blocks needed for positive and safe relationships, of all kinds, are taught and thoroughly understood by all children. This will start with family and friends, how to treat each other with kindness, and recognising the difference between online and offline friendships.
The government recommend that Sex Education be taught in primary schools where it is tailored to the age, physical and emotional maturity of the pupils. Our Relationship and Sex Policy includes the curriculum overview so parents / carers can follow their child’s learning journey.
You cannot withdraw your child from Relationships Education because it is important that all children receive this content, covering topics such as friendships and how to stay safe. If you do not want your child to take part in the reproduction objectives set out in the PSHE curriculum overview, you can ask that they are withdrawn. The Headteacher must grant this request. We ask that you discuss with us your reasons for this. The science curriculum also includes content on human development, including reproduction, which is statutory.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Copperfield Academy!
At Copperfield Academy, our children are at the heart of everything we do.
“Children are our Priority, Change is the Reality, Collaboration is our Strategy.”
We are proud to share that this commitment has been recognised in our most recent Ofsted inspection.
Here’s What Makes Us Special:
Children at the Centre: Our diverse and multicultural school prioritizes the needs of our students.Strong Foundations: Our Nursery and Reception classes are filled with energy and enthusiasm, giving children a flying start.Pride in Our School: Our pupils take pride in their school and their work, creating a positive atmosphere.Engaged Learners: Students listen intently to their teachers, fostering a culture of respect and learning.Positive Behaviour: Our pupils are well-behaved, friendly, and enjoy all that school has to offer.Camaraderie and Teamwork: A strong sense of community prevails, where everyone feels valued and supported.Celebrating Differences: Our students embrace diversity and support one another, creating an inclusive environment.Safety and Well-Being: The well-being and safety of our pupils are our top priorities, ensuring a vibrant, calm, and purposeful learning atmosphere.
At Copperfield Academy, we see each child as a unique individual. We focus on developing effective social and communication skills, preparing them to be caring, respectful citizens in our diverse world.
Building a Strong Community
We are dedicated to fostering a family-like community, collaborating with parents and carers to equip our children to be lifelong learners and responsible citizens who contribute positively to society.We believe that every child can achieve their best. Intelligence is not fixed; with the right challenges, there are no limits to what they can achieve. Each day, we strive to provide high-quality teaching and learning experiences.
Our REAch2 Touchstones—Enjoyment, Inclusion, Inspiration, Integrity, Learning, Leadership, and Responsibility—guide our expectations and interactions within our school and the broader community.
A Lifelong Learning Journey
We view learning as a lifelong process, where we are all committed to growing and improving. Our mission, “Challenge and Aspiration – Learning for Life!”, encapsulates this belief.Education is crucial for your child’s future success. Through our ethos, “The Copperfield Way,” our structured curriculum, and values-led assemblies, we nurture character and aim for every child to thrive.We are proud to be a school that upholds high expectations and supports our community.
We look forward to welcoming you to Copperfield Academy!

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision, Values and Aims – Copperfield Academy
pageCache.text:
Our Vision, Values and Aims
To inspire excellence in learning, leadership, and community through high expectations and meaningful relationships.
To cultivate a thriving community where excellence in learning, leadership, and relationships empowers every individual to reach their full potential.
We are committed to nurturing a culture of excellence by setting high expectations, fostering meaningful relationships, and empowering every learner and leader to thrive within a supportive and inclusive community.
A ‘Core Learning Value’ (CLV) is the focus of every whole-school assembly at the start of each week.
At Copperfield Academy, we are committed to promoting and upholding the British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. These values are integral to our school ethos and underpin all aspects of school life.
We encourage our pupils to engage in the democratic process, understanding the importance of their voice and the value of participation. Through Pupil Parliament elections and discussions, children learn how to express their opinions and contribute to decision-making in our school community.
We promote respect for the law and the importance of rules in our everyday lives. Our children are taught that laws are designed to protect and support everyone, and we foster an understanding of the consequences of breaking rules, both in school and in society.
We value each child’s right to make choices and express their views freely. Our curriculum empowers pupils to make informed decisions and understand the importance of personal responsibility. We celebrate individuality and encourage our students to develop their own identities while respecting others.
Respect is a core value at Copperfield Academy. We foster an environment where all members of our school community are treated with kindness and consideration. Our children learn the importance of respecting others’ opinions, beliefs, and backgrounds, creating a harmonious and supportive atmosphere.
Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs
We embrace diversity and promote inclusion among our children. Through education about various cultures, faiths, and beliefs, we encourage understanding and acceptance. Our aim is to prepare our children for life in a multicultural society, fostering a sense of belonging for everyone.
At Copperfield Academy, we strive to instill these British Values in our children, ensuring they become responsible, respectful, and active citizens who contribute positively to society.
Printed copies available on request via the main school office.

Early Explorers - Baby & Toddler Group
Every Wednesday (Term Time Only) | 2:00 PM – 3:00 PM | Copperfield Academy
Looking for a friendly, supportive space for you and your little one? Early Explorers is the perfect place to play, learn, and connect!Our group is designed for parents, carers, babies, and toddlers to enjoy quality time together while building a strong sense of community.
Each session includes:Fun, age-appropriate activities to help your child explore and develop through play.Opportunities to meet other adults, share experiences, and make lasting friendships.A safe, welcoming environment where everyone feels included.
Every other week, we invite special guest speakers to provide practical advice and support on topics that matter to families, such as:Paediatric First Aid – Learn essential skills to keep your child safe.Mental Health & Wellbeing – Tips for managing stress and supporting emotional health.Food Bank Support – Guidance on accessing local resources.Healthy Food Prep – Simple, nutritious ideas for busy families.
Why join us?Build confidence as a parent or carer.Access expert advice in a relaxed setting.Give your child the chance to socialise and play.
Interested in joining?Please contact the main school office ([email protected]) to register your interest. We look forward to welcoming you and your little explorers!

About REAch2
REAch2
Founded in 2012, REAch2 Academy Trust is the largest primary-only academy trust in the country. It is a growing charitable organisation currently supporting some 55 primary academies across England.
The Cornerstone of REAch2 is a solid, unshakeable foundation, defined by exceptional teaching experiences and shared Touchstone values of learning, leadership, enjoyment, inclusion, inspiration, responsibility and integrity.
These values are at the very core of the Trust, firmly embedded in all of our academies and embraced by our leaders, teachers, staff, parents and children alike.
Strong family values are a key component of the REAch2 vision. We believe that REAch2 is a family: connected by a common desire to learn from each other, share experiences and be mutually supportive across the entire academy community. Every school and every individual is included in this vision. We actively encourage collaboration – and work as a team to create and deliver the best possible educational experiences for every pupil within the REAch2 Trust.
If you would like to read more about REAch2 please following the link – http://reach2.org/

Career Related Learning
Career-related learning at Copperfield Academy is about opening up a world of opportunities for our children. We want to show our children that opportunities are endless, exposing them to a wide range of experiences, by encouraging them to understand that they can be anything they want to be, regardless of their gender, ethnicity or where they live.
Our career-related learning has been designed to motivate and fire the imagination of our children, especially when it comes to learning. Our pedagogy linked to aspirations allows the children to learn more about their own abilities and talents and see the links between their learning and their future.
If you would like to find out more about career-related learning – here are a few suggestions and resources that could help you inspire you children at home!
The BBC has a series of short films introducing a variety of careers, and the book series Little People, Big Dreams and Little Leaders introduce young readers to inspiring people from diverse backgrounds across a range of disciplines. Young, Gifted and Black by Jamia Wilson also lists 52 icons from the past and present to empower the next generation of changemakers.
Thinking about the future
This is an ideal link to introduce pupils to the world of work.
– My World of Work is a digital tool to help children find out more about which jobs might suit them
– The DfE’s Activity Passport is a helpful checklist to encourage your students to learn new skills and try out new hobbies
– A New Direction’s Learning Lenses resources developed through the Steve McQueen Year 3 project have some discussion and drama ideas. Start with I am Excellent and Strike a Pose from the Snapshots unit, and then follow on with Superheroes of the Future from the Selfies unit
